author: Zachary Bott
title: Pankratz, Cavs surge past Augusta Athletics - NewsBreak
text:
By Zachary Bott ,
6 hours ago
Eau Claire Cavaliers coach Ryan Bembnister enjoys himself a big offensive inning.
Whether it’s via the long ball or death by singles, Bembnister could care less.
It sure shows in his team, as the Cavs proved on a hazy Wednesday night at Carson Park by winning 15-5 over the Augusta Athletics.
“It was a nice win,” Bembnister said. “Augusta's fun to play. They're a scrappy team to play. We knew they wouldn't go away, and luckily, we had put enough runs on them.”
The Cavs improved to 10-5, while Augusta dropped to 0-17.
Cavs got to work early on Augusta and Fall Creek High School pitcher Josh Wright.
A walk, error and infield single loaded the bags for Sam Knickerbocker in the first.
The Saint Mary’s University Of Minnesota catcher got jammed, but muscled the ball enough into left field for a two-RBI single.
Two batters later, Eau Claire North alum Aiden Pankratz dribbled a ball up the middle for two RBI of his own.
The Cavs also made use of three Augusta errors as they batted around the order for a six-run first inning.
“We have guys that put the ball in play more often than not,” Bembnister said. “We always say create chaos in the base paths. You start getting the other team nervous. You start making them make mistakes, like you saw tonight, and you just roll into six-run innings.”
“It's got to be one of the better feelings in baseball putting up those big innings,” Pankratz said. “Hitting's contagious sometimes, and a couple hits here and there will just spark something, and everyone will start hitting well.”
Another big Cavs inning followed in the third.
Pankratz and Reilly Gapinski each led off with singles. Two more Athletics misplays brought them around and led to a four-run frame.
Keeping in tune with the big odd innings continued in the fifth, Pankratz capped off a team-leading three-hit night with his third RBI on a single.
“I was just trying to stay simple,” Pankratz said of his approach Wednesday. “See a fastball. And then, (when) they give me a fastball, swing at that and put it where they're not.”
“Situationally, batting wise, he knows where to put the ball and puts the ball in play a lot,” Bembnister said. “(He) reads pitchers really well. He's a model of what the Cavs are.”
Gapinski followed with a two-RBI single in a five-run Cavs frame that gave them 15 hits overall Wednesday.
Knickerbocker also had three hits and two RBI.
The run support allowed Cavs starter Mason Yarrington to pitch with a sense of comfort, as he went 5.1 innings with four strikeouts, allowing just one run for the win.
“The plan for him was keep him under 85 (pitches) that way he can come back on Sunday and pitch,” Bembnister said. “So, he did his job.”
The Cavs now will focus on Friday night’s Chippewa Rivers Baseball League South Division-deciding doubleheader with division rival Osseo Merchants, who are 8-6 after a loss Wednesday to the Eau Claire Bears.
“I think it's going to be really fun,” Pankratz said. “Osseo is a good team, and we're a good team. I'm hoping (it’s) a good battle.”
“The guys are laser-focused,” Bembnister said. “You can see them in the dugout; the energy was there, the approach was there, the defense was behind them.
“I reminded them that I've been coaching this team for five years and I've never won a conference title. It would mean a lot to me, but I think it means more to these guys.”
